lines.text: Everything on this ship gets cooked in the end. Salt pork today, brine tomorrow.
lines.journalNote: Bhima stirs his pots and speaks of the crew like cuts of meat. He knows everyone's appetite.

lines.text: The First Mate slipped below to the hold. Didn't carry flour, neither. There's cold steel in the air.
lines.journalNote: Bhima watched Kedar slip down the cargo hatch. Whispers of a gathering among the crates.

lines.text: Hear that shot? That was the Nakhuda's pistol. Kedar's taking the ship, and he won't be sharing the broth.
lines.journalNote: The captain is dead by Kedar's hand. Bhima is hunkered down, waiting out the butchery.

lines.text: The sea's got teeth! That's the Makara rising—wood won't hold it, prayers won't feed it!
lines.journalNote: The Leviathan has breached the port rail. Bhima screams that the ocean has come to swallow us whole.

lines.text: Look to the spar. When the white gull cries thrice, blood follows water. Never fails.
lines.journalNote: Bhima warned me of the gull's three cries. An ancient omen before every slaughter.

lines.text: Hari's watching the lifeboats. Give that dog a silver sovereign and he'll look at the clouds while you lower the davits.
lines.journalNote: Hari guards the starboard cutter, but his loyalty has a price: one gold coin to look away.

lines.text: Quartermaster! The salt beef is half gristle, but if you want the good rum from the captain's barrel, it'll cost you a shiny sovereign.
lines.journalNote: Bhima demands coin from the Quartermaster for anything beyond rotten salt beef.

lines.text: Navigator! Tell me we're steering toward calm shallows. Even my lentils are boiling sideways in this cursed water.
lines.journalNote: Bhima asked if the Navigator's charts show any end to this impossible sea.

lines.text: Here, lad, chew on a hard biscuit and don't let Kedar see you idling. Empty hands get cold steel on this ship.
lines.journalNote: Bhima slipped me a dry biscuit and warned me to stay out of the first mate's sights.

lines.text: Strange. The Captain's numbers are the only thing he never forgets.
lines.journalNote: Bhima whispered that Thorne's mind is gone, but his numbers stay burned in his skull.

lines.text: Stew doesn't stir itself, lad. I've told you what I know.
I told you already! Keep your nose out of my pots before you get scalded.
Are you deaf, swab? Back to your station before Kedar sees you idling!
The water in the stewpot hasn't boiled hot once since we crossed the third meridian. Unnatural cold.
You have that look again. Like a drowned rat that climbed back into the larder.
Salt pork and weevils. A ship full of men waiting to cut each other's throats.
I've sailed forty years under three flags. Never seen the tide run backwards before tonight.
Don't tap on the floorboards, boy. Whatever is singing under the hold doesn't like visitors.
If we go down, at least I won't have to scrape the grease off this copper kettle again.
Thorne hasn't eaten since dusk. Man's living on pistol powder and old grievances.
The gulls don't follow this ship anymore. Only that one solitary white bird on the yardarm.
Keep your boots dry if you can. Once the black water gets into your wool, it never leaves.
I keep hearing my mother's prayer in the wind. She died thirty leagues south of Goa.
Watch Kedar's eyes when he counts the casks. He's not counting brine, he's counting lives.
Every bell that strikes sounds like an iron coffin lid dropping shut.
